chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Kirdin al-Misma'i, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the hubara (a type of bird), and he said, 'I wish I had some of it, so I could eat from it until I was satisfied.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.أَتَمَلَّى: To be satisfied or full, indicating the act of eating until one's desire is met.
key_terms.الْحُبَارَى: Hubara, a specific type of bird known for its size and taste, often discussed in fiqh regarding its permissibility.

ai.seo_question: Is the hubara bird halal to eat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expresses a personal desire to consume the *hubara* bird until satisfied, serving as a strong indicator of its permissibility (halal) and culinary desirability in Shia jurisprudence. This statement reflects the scholarly principle that the Prophet’s and Imams’ enjoyment of a food item confirms its lawful status, distinguishing it from mere technical permissibility. The narration underscores the importance of animal sources in the dietary laws derived from the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing both ritual purity and gustatory pleasure.
